scope: Additive shared natural typing history through strict application Wasm, headless facade, immutable vanilla/React/durable sessions, browser intent boundaries and ordinary relay transport. Original defaults and protocols remain unchanged.

contracts.wasm: Exact native version 1, guarded enable/close/insert/deletion and separate grouped checkpoint/restore. Canonical decimal u64 clocks and closed bounded JSON. Stale/read-only checks precede payload parsing. Each new Rust action has its own documented file. Five top-level JS exports, 64 raw exports; no research exports.
contracts.ownership: Requested immutable history policy is explicit. Durable owners seal it after native admission, before initial save/mount. Older runtimes reject requested grouping/recovery instead of falling back. React rerenders preserve one owner; failed retirement hands off exact journal and declared history policy.
contracts.storage: IndexedDB version 1 and keys unchanged. Original sessions keep byte-identical strings. New records exactly declare breditor/shared-typing-checkpoint-record v1 plus checkpointJson. Default opens reject grouped records without overwriting; explicit opt-in atomically upgrades old journals while retaining old Undo/Redo. Failed first transaction keeps the original durable record and discards the unannounced owner.
contracts.publications: Changed native observations, not Boolean action outcomes, drive autosave. Fully invisible grouped Undo returns false but consumes history and changes publication; actual IDB bytes are checked after that publication. Read-only policy changes publication but is not restored permission.
contracts.dom: Only collapsed ordinary input and valid adjacent directional deletion use named user methods. Paste/composition/replacement/hardbreak/programmatic/format/move remain explicit. Pointer/navigation/blur/toolbar fences update cached native publication without repaint/focus. Owned asynchronous carets restore; outside focus/selection cannot overwrite Rust selection. Composition holds incoming frames.
contracts.relayRepair: A deterministic installed startup failure reproduced in every engine: SharedRelaySync constructor still called the original-only checkpoint identity check. It now selects the family from the native view, preserving exact room/writer/model/byte checks and original writer-stream semantics. New unit rejects wrong writers in both modes. No codec fallback, new wire operation or engine patch.
contracts.limits: Existing 16 MiB/1000-journal-entry/64-input/750ms native limits remain. No dependency, vendor source, original model/journal/factory or default browser contract is changed.

timingConcern.kind: Unqualified wall-clock observation, not an approved benchmark
timingConcern.interpretation: Input gaps exceeded 750ms under qualification load, so native history correctly splits. This is a serious responsiveness concern, not a repaired product behavior. Browser assertions use captured actual clocks; separate real-Wasm tests prove <=750/>750 behavior above 2^53. No window/deadline increase or retry hides it. Profile the native staged-for-typing whole-journal replay and surrounding work without weakening atomicity.

These are test executions, not unique product capabilities.
